headline: Meta surveilled former exec to enforce silence on her memoir
summary: Former Meta director Sarah Wynn-Williams sues, claiming the company violated her free speech rights and used financial duress to prevent her from promoting her book "Careless People."
details: A former Meta executive is suing the company, alleging that Meta attempted to silence her and enforce a non-disparagement agreement through financial duress. Sarah Wynn-Williams, who authored the memoir "Careless People," claims Meta's actions are invalid and aimed at preventing her from promoting her book.

Wynn-Williams, who served as director of global public policy at Facebook (now Meta) from 2011 to 2017, alleges that the company obtained an emergency gag order against her. This order reportedly bars her and her lawyers from criticizing Meta or discussing her book.

The lawsuit states that Meta is seeking $50,000 in damages for each alleged violation of the non-disparagement agreement. Wynn-Williams argues this financial pressure constitutes duress and is asking the court to lift the arbitration order and vacate her severance agreement.

According to the lawsuit, Meta has been surveilling Wynn-Williams for over a year, with company representatives attending her public appearances and photographing her. The lawsuit claims this surveillance was conducted "to document that at each event, Ms. Wynn-Williams said nothing about Meta or her book."

Meta has countered that Wynn-Williams violated her agreement and that her book contains inaccuracies. The company stated that the former employee is using the legal process to sell books, a claim an arbitrator previously ruled against her on. Meta asserts her book is "divorced from reality, disparaging and riddled with false claims."

The lawsuit further alleges that Meta took issue with Wynn-Williams attending an arts and literary festival in the UK, where she was on a panel but remained silent because other panelists were critics of the company. The suit claims Meta's actions are an attempt to "strike fear into the heart of anyone else who dares to consider speaking the truth about Meta’s unlawful and abusive practices."

headline_marked: Instagram testing [[more ways to customize 'Your Algorithm']]
headline: Instagram testing more ways to customize 'Your Algorithm'
summary: The social media giant is exploring new methods for users to control the content they see, aiming to make feed personalization more central to the experience.
details: Instagram head Adam Mosseri has revealed that the platform is testing new features to give users greater control over their content feeds. These updates aim to evolve the 'Your Algorithm' setting from a hidden option into a core part of the user experience.

The proposed changes include pulling down on the feed to access the 'Your Algorithm' menu, or swiping up from a Reel to bring up customization prompts. Additionally, buttons under each Reel could allow users to directly indicate preferences for similar content.

While Instagram is expanding its algorithm customization tools, many users are expressing a clear desire for a simpler feed. The most frequent comment on Mosseri's announcement is a plea to prioritize content from accounts users actually follow.
